a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Measured absolute oral bioavailability in the most relevant L1 contexts is well above the 20% threshold: diclofenac ~50%, lumiracoxib ~74%, BI 425809 ~71.6%, and indomethacin SR ~76-80%.

The query is an acidic, moderately lipophilic, drug-sized sulfonamide; related acidic NSAID and sulfonamide/isoxazole-containing molecules in these records achieve F >= 20% despite ionizable/acidic character, so ionization is not affirmative evidence for F < 20%.
No L1 record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence of F < 20%; all active-context measured mean values are >= 49%, and the F >= 20% threshold is modest.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule.
No matched oral versus IV exposure data for the query.
No experimental permeability, solubility, or first-pass metabolism data for the query.
Transfer from analogs is indirect; structural differences such as the benzodioxole, thiophene sulfonamide, and isoxazole may alter absorption or metabolism.
Some related records show wide interpatient variability, but mean values remain above the 20% threshold.
content.decision_summary: Prediction high: all transferable L1 records show F >= 49% for related acidic NSAIDs and sulfonamide/isoxazole-containing drugs, and the query's ionization/TPSA liabilities are not affirmative evidence for F < 20%; F >= 20% is better supported.
